name: Episodic
description: Connected but semi-independent episodes sharing characters and setting, linked by an overarching thread or theme. Each episode tells a self-contained mini-story while advancing the larger narrative. Well-suited for character-driven stories, journey narratives, and anthology-style tales.

framework.overarching_thread: A unifying element that connects all episodes: a quest, a relationship arc, a mystery being unraveled piece by piece, or a thematic question being explored from different angles.
framework.episode_independence: Each episode should be satisfying on its own — with its own conflict, stakes, and resolution — while also contributing to the larger story.
framework.character_continuity: The protagonist develops across episodes. Each episode should reveal something new about them or advance their growth.

phases.label: Prologue — Setting the Stage
phases.purpose: Establish the protagonist, the overarching situation, and the thread that will connect all episodes. Set up the journey, quest, or central question.
phases.guidance: Introduce the protagonist with a clear desire, need, or mission. Establish the world. Hint at the scope of what is to come. This is not a full episode — it is the launch pad.

phases.label: Episode 1 — First Encounter
phases.purpose: The first standalone episode. Introduces a new situation, character, or challenge. Establishes the episodic pattern.
phases.guidance: This episode sets the template for the story's rhythm. Give it a clear beginning, middle, and end. The protagonist should learn something or gain something that carries forward. Introduce the first piece of the overarching puzzle.

phases.label: Episode 2 — Deepening
phases.purpose: A second episode that deepens the story. Raise the stakes, reveal new facets of the protagonist, or introduce a complication to the overarching thread.
phases.guidance: Vary the tone or type of conflict from Episode 1. If the first was action-oriented, this could be more emotional or cerebral. Show character growth. Advance the overarching thread.

phases.label: Episode 3 — Complication
phases.purpose: The overarching thread thickens. This episode introduces a major complication, reversal, or revelation that connects back to earlier episodes.
phases.guidance: Raise the overarching stakes significantly. Earlier events or characters may recur with new significance. The protagonist faces a harder challenge that tests their growth.

phases.label: Episode 4 — Crisis
phases.purpose: The most intense episode. The overarching conflict reaches a peak within this episode's specific scenario. The protagonist is truly tested.
phases.guidance: This episode should feel like the culmination of what came before. The episodic conflict and the overarching conflict intersect. Maximum emotional and narrative intensity.

phases.label: Epilogue — Threads United
phases.purpose: Resolve the overarching thread. Show how the cumulative experiences across all episodes have transformed the protagonist. Bring closure.
phases.guidance: Connect the dots. Show how each episode contributed to the protagonist's transformation or the resolution of the central question. End with resonance — a final image or insight that unifies the whole.

each_episode_contains: A specific setting or situation (can be new or recurring)
A local conflict with its own stakes and resolution
At least one new or recurring secondary character
A moment of protagonist development or revelation
A contribution to the overarching thread (clue, lesson, relationship, or piece of the puzzle)
episode_structure.episode_pacing: Each episode should have its own mini-arc: setup → conflict → escalation → resolution. The resolution of each episode should raise a question or create momentum for the next.

section_distribution_guidance: The prologue and epilogue are typically one section each. Each episode can be one or two sections depending on total word count. For 6 sections: prologue, 4 episodes, epilogue. For 8 sections: prologue, 4 episodes (some spanning 2 sections), epilogue. For 10+ sections: prologue, 5-6 episodes, epilogue.
voiceover_notes: Episode transitions should feel natural, not jarring. Use time transitions ('Three days later...'), spatial transitions ('The road led to a village unlike any they had seen'), or thematic bridges. Each episode should open with a fresh hook. The episodic structure is excellent for voiceover because it provides natural variety and regular moments of satisfaction.
